title: Geometry & Mensuration
tagline: Triangles, circles, solids, trig, coordinate geometry — draw first, formula second.

subsections.title: Triangles
subsections.trick: Apollonius’ Theorem is the fastest route to a median length — don’t drop a perpendicular and use Pythagoras twice. For area, pick the formula that matches what’s given: base+height, all 3 sides (Heron), two sides+included angle, or inradius+semi-perimeter. For a right triangle, skip Heron's formula entirely: r=(a+b−c)/2 and R=c/2 (half the hypotenuse) — both come straight from the leg lengths. For an equilateral triangle inscribed/circumscribed pair, R=2r always (from the 2:1 centroid split), so area ratios are always 4:1.

pyqs.q: A right triangle has sides 15, 20, 25 cm. Find inradius : circumradius.
pyqs.a: No need for Heron's formula — use the right-triangle shortcuts directly: r=(15+20−25)/2=5, R=25/2=12.5. Ratio = ×2:5.

pyqs.q: An equilateral triangle is inscribed in a circle of radius R; another circle is inscribed in the triangle. Find (outer circle area) : (inner circle area).
pyqs.a: The centroid splits every median 2:1, and that same point is both the circumcentre and incentre of an equilateral triangle — so R = 2r automatically. Since area ∝ radius², the ratio is 2²:1² = ×4:1, with zero computation needed.

pyqs.q: Triangle ABC has AB=AC=50 cm, BC=80 cm. Find the sum of all three altitudes.
pyqs.a: Altitude to BC (the base) via Pythagoras on the half-base: √(50²−40²)=30 cm → Area=½×80×30=1200. The other two altitudes both equal 2×Area/50 = 48 cm (equal, since the triangle is isosceles). Sum = 30+48+48 = ×126 cm.

subsections.title: Polygons
subsections.trick: Exterior angles of any convex polygon always sum to 360° regardless of the number of sides — use that before the interior-angle formula, it's one less step.

pyqs.q: ABCDEF is a regular hexagon; P, Q are midpoints of AB, CD. Find (area of trapezium PBCQ) : (area of hexagon).
pyqs.a: Split the regular hexagon into 6 equilateral triangles from the centre; PBCQ covers a clean fraction of that total once you place P and Q as midpoints and add up the relevant triangle/trapezium pieces symbolically — comes out to ×5:24.

subsections.title: Circles
subsections.trick: Power-of-a-point (PA×PB = PC×PD, or PT² for a tangent) solves almost every ‘two chords/tangent meet outside a circle’ question in one line — no need to find angles first. Count common tangents by picturing the two-circle case: apart →4, intersecting →2, internally touching →1, one inside the other →0.

pyqs.q: Circle radius 26 cm; parallel chords PQ and SR with ∠PQC=45° and distance ratio 3:2 from center. Find area of quadrilateral PQRS.
pyqs.a: ∠PQC=45° means the triangle from centre to the chord's midpoint and endpoint is right-isosceles, so d₁ = 26/√2 = 13√2 immediately (no trig table needed). Scale d₂ by the given 3:2 ratio, find both chord lengths via Pythagoras, then treat PQRS as a trapezium: Area = ×20(34+3√14) sq. cm.

pyqs.q: Tangents PQ, PR touch a circle at Q, R. A separate tangent AB touches with ∠AOB=50°. Find ∠APB.
pyqs.a: For any external point with two tangents to a circle, the angle between the tangents and the central angle to the tangent points are supplementary: ∠APB = 180°−2×∠AOB. Here that's 180−100 = ×80°.

subsections.title: Mensuration — 2D Figures
subsections.trick: For a trapezium/quadrilateral with a diagonal + two altitudes given, split into two triangles rather than hunting for a single formula — the table formula is just that split pre-done.

formulas.label: Path across the middle of a rectangle

pyqs.q: A rhombus has side 36 cm and area 396 sq. cm. Find |d₁−d₂|.
pyqs.a: Use d₁²+d₂² = 4a² = 5184 (from the side) and d₁d₂ = 792 (from 2×Area). Then (d₁−d₂)² = (d₁²+d₂²) − 2d₁d₂ = 5184−1584 = 3600 — no need to solve for d₁ and d₂ individually. |d₁−d₂| = ×60 cm.

subsections.title: Mensuration — Solids
subsections.trick: Volume scales with the cube of linear size, surface area with the square — if a solid is scaled by k, volume ×k³ and surface area ×k². Saves recomputing from scratch on ‘melted and recast’ questions.

formulas.label: Right prism
formulas.latex: LSA = (\text{perimeter of base})\times h, \quad V = (\text{area of base})\times h

formulas.label: Right circular cylinder
formulas.latex: LSA = 2\pi rh, \quad TSA = 2\pi r(r+h), \quad V = \pi r^2 h

formulas.label: Right pyramid
formulas.latex: LSA = \tfrac{1}{2}(\text{perimeter of base})\times(\text{slant height}), \quad V = \tfrac{1}{3}(\text{area of base})\times h

formulas.label: Right circular cone
formulas.latex: LSA=\pi r\ell, \quad TSA=\pi r(\ell+r), \quad V=\tfrac{1}{3}\pi r^2h, \quad \ell=\sqrt{r^2+h^2}

formulas.label: Hemisphere
formulas.latex: LSA=2\pi r^2, \quad TSA=3\pi r^2, \quad V=\tfrac{2}{3}\pi r^3

pyqs.q: A solid metal cylinder of radius 6 cm and height 12 cm is melted and recast into cones of radius 3 cm and height 4 cm each. How many cones are formed?
pyqs.a: Volume is conserved on melting — just divide cylinder volume by cone volume: (π×6²×12) ÷ (⅓π×3²×4) = 432π ÷ 12π = ×36 cones. No need to track any other dimension once you set up the ratio.

subsections.title: Trigonometry
subsections.trick: “School | After — To | College”: reading the 2×2 quadrant grid like a page, that's the order All / Sin / Tan / Cos are positive going anticlockwise from Q1. For standard angles, know sin·cos·tan at 0°/30°/45°/60°/90° cold — deriving them costs too much time mid-exam.

formulas.label: tan in terms of sin, cos

pyqs.q: A tower's shadow is √3 times its height. Find the sun's angle of elevation.
pyqs.a: tanθ = height/shadow = 1/√3 → θ = ×30° — recognise the 1/√3 ratio from the standard-angles table instantly rather than computing arctan.

subsections.title: Coordinate Geometry
subsections.trick: The shoelace-style area formula works even when the triangle looks 'obviously' irregular — no need to identify base/height on a coordinate grid. For perpendicular distance from the origin specifically, skip x₁,y₁ entirely and use c/√(a²+b²) directly. For 'circle given as x²+y²+2gx+2fy+c=0', just plug the external point straight into that expression — it IS the tangent-length formula, no need to find the centre and radius first.

formulas.label: Perpendicular distance from a point to a line
Length of tangent from an external point to a circle

pyqs.q: Find the length of the tangent from (5,6) to the circle x²+y²−4x−6y+4=0.
pyqs.a: Plug straight into L=√(x₁²+y₁²+2gx₁+2fy₁+c) using the equation's own coefficients (2g=−4, 2f=−6, c=4): L=√(25+36−20−36+4)=√9 = ×3 units.
